before.exam_tip_html: When describing the production of monoclonal antibodies, examiners want you to include all five steps in order: inject antigen into mouse → extract lymphocytes → fuse with tumour cells → form hybridoma → select, clone and collect. A common mistake is forgetting to explain why tumour cells are used (they divide indefinitely). For 6-mark extended response questions, always link the use of monoclonal antibodies back to their specificity — they work because each one binds to only one type of antigen.

For calculation questions using p = hρg, always check your units — h must be in metres, ρ in kg/m³, and g in N/kg to get pressure in pascals. For “explain” questions about gas pressure, always refer to particles, collisions, and force — the examiners want you to use the particle model, not just say “pressure goes up.” For Boyle’s law calculations, write out p1V1 = p2V2 and substitute carefully before rearranging.
